verbalization: The visible evidence suggests a potential relationship between Myristelaidic acid and the EZH2/SUZ12/EED complex, mediated through the intermediate target Low affinity cationic amino acid transporter 2. Myristelaidic acid is reported to have low affinity for this transporter, which is itself a target of Epicoccin T. Epicoccin T, in turn, is implicated in targeting the EZH2/SUZ12/EED complex. This pathway implies a possible mechanism by which Myristelaidic acid may influence the activity of the EZH2 complex, though the direct interaction remains uncertain. The scores indicate a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, supported by the sequential targeting of the three entities. The evidence highlights a potential regulatory pathway involving cationic amino acid transport and epigenetic modifiers, though further experimental validation is required to confirm the specific interaction.
